title: Bruises in different stages
objective: Recognize the five forms of elder abuse (physical, emotional, sexual, financial, neglect) and who is most at risk: people reliant on carers, living in institutional settings or under financial strain
secondaryObjectives: Include the caregiver's view as well as the patient's when building a falls-prevention plan for someone with cognitive impairment, which improves adherence and outcomes

brief.situation: 14:00 at Mrs. Ilic's home. You are the home health physical therapist on your fourth visit. She is 84, has mild cognitive impairment after a stroke, and depends on her son for meals, medicines and money. Today he answers every question for her and won't leave the room.
handover: Last visit she had a bruise on her left forearm 'from the walker'. Her refrigerator was nearly empty, and she said her bank card 'went missing'.

Agency policy and your state's law: health professionals who reasonably suspect abuse, neglect or exploitation of a vulnerable adult report to Adult Protective Services the same day; call 911 if the person is in immediate danger; tell your supervisor.
howItWorks: The clock runs in simulated time; study pace runs three simulated minutes per real minute. Pause any time.
Each check takes the time on its button. Decide what the findings mean, what to stop or start, and who must know.
Partway through you are asked to write your reasoning. A debrief scores what you did.

why.question: What do you suspect, and what do you do?

parts.label: What and why
parts.criteria: Grip bruises of different ages, a caregiver who controls the conversation, weight loss, missed medicines and a missing bank card suggest physical abuse, neglect and financial exploitation of a woman who depends on her carer.
parts.modelAnswer: This looks like abuse: grip-mark bruises of different ages, a son who won't let her talk, weight loss, missed pills and her bank card gone. She depends on him for everything.

parts.label: What I do
parts.criteria: Sees her alone, asks about safety, avoids confronting the son, reports to Adult Protective Services the same day (911 if in immediate danger), tells the supervisor and documents objectively.
parts.modelAnswer: Get her alone and ask if she's safe, don't confront him, report to APS today, 911 if she's in immediate danger, tell my supervisor and document exactly what I saw and heard.

scoring.modelReasoning: Elder abuse takes physical, emotional, sexual, financial and neglect forms; those most at risk rely on carers, live in institutions or are under financial strain. Red flags include bruises in various stages of healing, a caregiver who will not let the person speak alone, dehydration and malnutrition, and unauthorized use of their money. See her alone, ask about safety, avoid confronting the suspected abuser, report to Adult Protective Services in her state (911 for immediate danger), tell your supervisor and document objectively.
